Eight briefs, one hand, twelve visual languages.

An illustration portfolio built around a single question: can the same hand render film noir and vaporwave with equal conviction? Eight self-initiated concept projects, each built as a real commercial brief rather than a style exercise.

Neon Dynasty → Genre Atlas 12 required styles, 8 projects
01 / 08 Album artwork + tour poster

Neon Dynasty

Self-initiated concept project

Cover art for a fictional synthwave act, Chrome Ascension — a lone figure climbing a rain-lit stairwell toward a floating corporate spire, dissolving into digital noise as they rise. Built through layered digital painting with hand-placed glitch artifacts rather than a filter pass, so the corruption reads as intentional rather than accidental.

02 / 08 Book cover series, 3 covers

The Velvet Alibi

Self-initiated concept project

A hardboiled detective trilogy for a fictional publisher, Cross & Vane Press. Three covers sharing one recurring visual device — a venetian-blind shadow-slat motif — so the set reads as a series on a shelf, a constraint that forced restraint in a genre that tempts overrendering.

03 / 08 Character illustration + game concept art

Aurelia's Clockwork Menagerie

Self-initiated concept project

Concept art for a fictional narrative game — a clockmaker-inventor and her three brass mechanical creatures. The test for myself: whether Art Nouveau's organic ornament could soften steampunk's usual grim-industrial read without losing the mechanical logic. Every gear still has to plausibly turn.

SteampunkArt nouveau Clip Studio PaintProcreate
Process — mechanical owl constructionConcept render
Process: silhouette exploration for the protagonist and each creature, line-of-action construction sketches, material studies for brass/leather/glass, then final render.
04 / 08 Editorial illustration

The Architect's Dream

Self-initiated concept project

For a fictional culture magazine, Meridian — a feature on "cities we only visit in dreams." A grand Art Deco train station where the platforms fold upward into staircases leading into open sky. Deco's obsessive symmetry is the argument here: it can make an impossible space feel inevitable rather than strange.

SurrealArt deco IllustratorPhotoshop
Hero — main illustrationConcept render
Process — perspective wireframeConcept render
Process: vector perspective/construction wireframe, thumbnail composition variants, a value study, then the final color pass.
05 / 08 Brand identity + event poster

Signal Loss // Ghost FM

Self-initiated concept project

A mini brand system for a fictional late-night internet radio station. The glitch here is choreographed, not accidental — every scan line and channel-split is placed by hand so the "broken signal" still reads as legible brand design, not noise for its own sake.

Brand mark — clean vectorConcept render
Process: grid/layout sketch, three type-lockup iterations, then a before/after glitch-technique breakdown.
06 / 08 Packaging + label system

Amber Soda Co.

Self-initiated concept project

A label system, not a single illustration — three flavors for a fictional heritage soda brand sharing one illustration technique and one layout grid, the kind of constraint real packaging work actually runs on.

Genre Atlas

Self-initiated concept project

One frame, twelve languages. A genre-category key-art system for a fictional streaming platform — the same composition, the same character scale, rendered honestly in each of the twelve required aesthetics. This is the direct answer to "can you actually shift style, not just mood."
